input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
input.rationale: Section 22.1 grants unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems — squarely in walk-away territory and failing the fallback on frequency, notice and system access. It also conflicts with § 22.2, which bars direct access to Customer systems. Cost allocation in § 22.2 (Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%) and confidentiality of findings in § 22.3 already meet the preferred position, so the redline only fixes frequency, notice and access in § 22.1.

proposal.summary: Limit Vendor audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, off-site via an independent auditor, and delete remote system access.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We limited audits to one off-site audit per 12 months on 30 days' written notice during business hours by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and removed remote access to our systems, consistent with our playbook position and § 22.2's existing bar on direct system access. We can accept 15 days' notice if that helps.

ops.oldText: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
ops.newText: Vendor may audit Customer's usage no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, on at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, during Customer's normal business hours and with minimal disruption, and such audit shall be conducted off-site by an independent auditor bound by written obligations of confidentiality. Vendor and its auditor shall have no remote or direct access to Customer's systems, and Customer shall instead provide relevant usage records reasonably required for the audit.
